body:
maria: Heads-up — after the 4821 kernel/driver bump we saw a ~12% p99 increase on L40S for the longctx suite. Can folks help run a quick head-to-head with H100/A100/L40S so we can decide whether to rollback or tune?

ajay: ack. which model and which benchmark? small quick sweep or full longctx?

maria: model: redwood/ggml-13B-like, seq=4/512/2048, batch=1. The regression shows up at seq=2048 p99 and some microbursts at 512. Quick sweep is fine — we just need a reproducible tie-breaker.

ramon: saw similar on my dev rack — L40S temps spiked a bit on long runs and driver logged a couple thermal warnings. worth checking power caps and nvlink config.

perf-bot: Automated summary for 1767504321: baseline(H100)->p99=38ms, L40S-before->p99=34ms, L40S-after->p99=38.1ms. Full logs: https://internal.perf/bench/1767504321

olivia: @maria is the workload using KV cache heavily? KV/cache warming differences can change p99 a lot on L40S.

maria: KV cache yes — chat-style token stream. But the microburst pattern looks like kernel fallback (thinbatch->fallback path) which the kernel change might have touched. PR to investigate is https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821

ajay: I'll run the mini-bakeoff tonight across three SKUs. Can you confirm exact bench command and the env so I don't miscompare?

maria: use bench harness: `tools/bench/run_longctx.sh --model ggml-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --iters 200 --tag mini-bakeoff-1767`

Also run with and without KV cache: `--kv-cache on|off`. Record p50/p95/p99 and include `--trace kernel` logs.

ajay: got it. I'll set up two runs per SKU (kv on/off), seed=42, and 200 iters. Putting jobs in overnight queue `ovrnight-small-sweep`. Will post raw csvs.

ramon: add one more: disable the thinbatch fallback plugin to force the optimized path so we can isolate kernel fallback behavior: `--disable-thin-fallback`

maria: good catch. include that as a variant. If L40S still regresses with fallback disabled then it's likely a scheduling/thermal thing.

devops: FYI I'm pinning a node pool with firmware v3.2.1 and power cap 300W for the L40S runs to reduce thermal variance — name: `l40s-stable-300w-1767`.

ajay: quick note — I saw a spurious NVML error on A100 once, rerunning that one now.

ajay: results (quick summary): H100 p99=36.8ms (kv on), A100 p99=39.1ms (kv on, one NVML retry), L40S p99=40.2ms (kv on, fallback enabled), L40S p99=35.0ms (kv on, fallback disabled). CSVs + kernel traces uploaded: https://internal.perf/uploads/1767504321/csvs.zip

maria: interesting — disabling fallback improved L40S a lot, suggests kernel fallback path is the offender. A100 noisy but close.

ramon: can you paste the kernel trace snippet for L40S fallback? curious which kernel call is slower.

ajay: snippet from trace (L40S fallback): ```
[2026-06-12T03:12:44Z] kernel_dispatch: thinbatch_fallback -> run_slow_kern
[2026-06-12T03:12:45Z] run_slow_kern: matmul_split (shard 3) took 14.2ms
[2026-06-12T03:12:45Z] kv_store: flush -> 1.8ms
```

olivia: that matmul_split spike smells like a kernel selection issue where the heuristic picked an unoptimized path. PR 4821 touched the selection heuristic around seq thresholds.

maria: ok next steps: ajay and ramon to repro with `--disable-thin-fallback` and `--kv-cache` variants, collect traces, and create a short comparision doc in /docs/perf/1767504321-mini. If reproducible, we either revert 4821 or patch the heuristic. Tag me when done.

ajay: will do. ETA morning, I'll ping here when uploads complete. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Job ovrnight-small-sweep completed for 1767504321. Artifacts: https://internal.perf/uploads/1767504321/csvs.zip (available)

ajay: done — uploads complete. left a short note in the csv README about the NVML retry on A100.

maria: thanks team. I'll open a hotfix PR to guard the heuristic with a canary. If the mini-bakeoff still shows issues after the hotfix we'll consider rollback.

ramon: thanks — I'll follow up on the thermal logs and node pool health.

olivia: ping me if you want me to run a quick model-agnostic microbench for kernel selection behavior. happy to help.

maria: appreciated. tagging @perf-bot for automated regression alert if p99 delta >10% in next sweep. :eyes:
